entries.reason: Single Responsibility — The spec addresses one concern: formalizing specId options across FlowStore, FlowManager, and the four CLI setters. All scope items, requirements, and tasks are directly related to that single concern. scope.out explicitly excludes unrelated changes.; Task Single Responsibility — T-1 covers FlowStore/FlowManager API formalization (a single coherent module pair), T-2 covers CLI setter specId threading (same operation across four setter files), and T-3 covers adding contract tests. No task title or acceptance list spans unrelated modules or concerns.; Unambiguous Requirements — No requirement uses vague adjectives such as 'appropriate', 'fast', or 'easy'. Each requirement states a concrete behavioral condition (e.g., 'must update specs/<specId>/flow.json when opts.specId is provided', 'must return without writing metrics and without throwing').; Complete Context — using the existing task scope rules — The phrase 'existing task scope rules' is not defined anywhere in the spec. Two independent reviewers cannot agree on whether an implementation satisfies R5 without examining external source code to discover those rules. (at requirements[4].desc); Complete Context — the entry taskId follows existing task scope rules — The acceptance criterion for R5 repeats 'existing task scope rules' without defining them, leaving no self-contained, verifiable condition against which reviewers can evaluate conformance. (at acceptance_criteria[3]); REQ Diff-Verifiability — All requirements are verifiable from a diff plus test execution: each describes concrete file targets (specs/<specId>/flow.json), method signatures, call-precedence rules, or no-op exit conditions that tests can assert directly. No requirement depends on extensibility contracts or out-of-diff process invariants.; No Hardcoded Secrets — The content is a spec document; no API keys, passwords, tokens, or other secrets appear.; No Silent Error Swallowing — Constraint #6 (Exit code contract) explicitly requires that invalid input, unknown taskId, absent flow.json, schema validation failure, and write failure produce Envelope.fail or a thrown error—preventing silent discard. R6 intentional no-op for absent specId/active-flow is an explicit design decision, not silent swallowing.; Prioritize Requirements — Eight requirements exceed the three-item threshold; every requirement carries an explicit priority field: R1–R7 are 'must' and R8 is 'should'.; Impact on Existing Features — Impact on existing features is explicitly addressed across the spec: R6 preserves ambient metric no-op, R7 preserves existing CLI validation, constraint[7] preserves active-flow fallback when ctx.specId is absent, clarification #4 states 'Existing behavior remains', and scope.out states that finalize/merge/cleanup semantics are unchanged.; Bounded Resource Usage — The spec does not introduce recursive processing, retries, or bulk data loading. Mutations target a single flow.json file per call, so no unbounded resource usage is present.; Spec Includes Test Strategy — R8 requires spec-local test coverage; each task (T-1, T-2, T-3) carries a dedicated test_strategy field specifying what to test and how; acceptance criteria require // spec: R<N> headers in specs/262-formalize-specid-opts/tests/.; Record Unresolved Points as Open Questions — open_questions is empty and the spec makes no claims about unresolved points. Decisions labeled [VERIFY] cite concrete evidence (file paths and code patterns) rather than fabricating answers.; Include 'Why This Approach' Rationale — The 'background' section explains why this approach is needed (gap from Spec 251), 'alternatives_considered' documents three rejected options with explicit reasons, and the 'decisions' section explains each key design choice with supporting evidence.; Spec Test Coverage — R8 (should priority) and the corresponding acceptance criterion explicitly require spec-local test files under specs/262-formalize-specid-opts/tests/ with '// spec: R<N>' headers for every testable requirement (R1–R8). T-3 reinforces this obligation.; Backward-Compatible CLI Interface — The acknowledged exception in $.constraints[7] includes the guardrail_id 'backward-compatible-cli-interface' and contains well over 20 non-whitespace characters after removing it ('既存コマンド名、位置引数、option の意味は変えない。ctx.specId がない環境では従来どおり current active flow を更新する。'). The rationale comes from constraints, satisfying the exception requirements.; Exit Code Contract — Constraint #6 (Exit code contract) explicitly states what constitutes success (ok:true / exit 0 for valid input and successful mutation) and failure (ok:false / non-zero for invalid input, unknown taskId, absent flow.json, schema validation failure, write failure) for every modified command.; Validate User Input at Entry Point — Constraint #5 lists each user-facing argument with validation requirements (text non-empty for request/note, positive integer for issue, existing VALID_PHASES/VALID_METRIC_COUNTERS for metric, existing taskId validation at entry point). ctx.specId is explicitly marked as an internal CLI context field, satisfying the 'mark internal arguments' requirement.
Spec gate failed because R5 referenced existing task scope rules without defining them in the spec.
entries.resolution: Rewrote R5 and acceptance criteria to enumerate taskId null, known id, unknown id, and absent taskId behavior.
